catalog_quote: (2) an even more important issue regarding stress for the history of Kelāsi is the exceptional stress pattern of feminine nouns in most NWI languages that have retained gender. That is, all masculine nouns (including proper names), all adjectives, postpositions, numerals, pronouns, most adverbs, all non-finite verbal forms (infinitives, participles) have one overall stress pattern: always on the final syllable, e.g., Kafteji berá 'brother', værzá 'ox', berénj 'rice (uncooked)', tævilæ 'stable', zæminlærzé 'earthquake', hæsæn 'Hasan', tehrán 'Tehran', šemæ 'you (plural)', hoštén 'self', delæ 'inside, within', kœnæ 'old', xorém 'good', dozzá 'twelve', ará 'tomorrow', pærirúz 'the day before yesterday', vatœn 'to say', bešnævessæn ... feminine nouns in those NWI that have an overt feminine (direct) marker – the full forms of Kafteji – have a different pattern: they are stressed on the penultimate syllable. While stress in Western Iranian languages may indeed shift away from word-final position when inflectional morphemes are at issue (e.g., unstressed possessive enclitics and indefinite suffixes and, for verbs, stress-attracting TAM prefixes, etc.), these stress patterns always appear in the context of morphology added to base forms via grammatical rules. Therefore, an exceptional stress pattern for base-form stems such as feminine nouns could be one plausible explanation for the loss of the unstressed feminine morpheme.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress in Kafteji (Kabatei) falls on the final syllable of the word for masculine nouns (incl. proper names), adjectives, postpositions, numerals, pronouns, most adverbs and non-finite verb forms; feminine nouns carrying the overt feminine direct marker (unstressed -a) are stressed on the penult, i.e. on the last syllable of the stem, so masculine and feminine forms can differ by stress alone.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing seen in the accessible snippets.
new_statements.exceptions: Feminine nouns with the overt (unstressed -a) feminine marker: penultimate stress (marker dropped in isolation/citation forms in Kafteji); stress shifts away from word-final position with unstressed possessive enclitics and indefinite suffixes; in finite verbs, stress-attracting TAM prefixes; 'most' (not all) adverbs final-stressed; a stress contrast distinguishes masculine vs feminine oblique forms.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress on citation/inflected word forms; the generalisation is framed for 'most NWI languages that have retained gender' and exemplified explicitly with Kafteji (Kabatei) words from Stilo's own fieldwork. Accessed only as Google Books snippets (saved) — full context and print page unverified.
new_statements.identity_note: Stilo's 'Kafteji' is the endonym-based name for Kabatei (ISO xkp, kaba1276), the Tatic variety of the village Kabateh (کَبَته; locally Kafte) in Rostamabad-e Jonubi rural district, Central district of Rudbar county, Gilan; its closest relative is Kelāsi of neighbouring Kalās (Stilo 1981 Group Four B, 'Taromi type'; Glottolog Taromic). Glottolog's coordinates (37.05 N 49.76 E) fall in Siahkal county and look approximate. The stress generalisation in Stilo 2019 is phrased for gender-retaining NW Iranian languages generally but is exemplified with Kafteji words from Stilo's own 1970s fieldwork.
